segments: Page 73. First dynasty of the Roman kings.
And then that King Leo fell into bowel pain and died.
Leo [the Great] was succeeded by Leontius {Leo II}.
When he had reigned one year,
and even his father Zeno was bowing down to him,
as to a child, his mother seduced him [with advice],
saying: "When your father bows down to you,
take the crown that is on your head,
and place it upon his head."
And when he did so,
Zeno seized the kingdom,
and made his son Leontius {Leo II} proëdros (proëdron, that is,
chief,
first?
shall he make [him] as hypateusis, hypatos,
consul? {glosses on the Greek term in OCR}).
And after a few days that boy died,
and many were offended [thinking]
that his father and his mother had killed him.
After Leontius, [Z]eno his father [reigned] fifteen years.
And when Verina, the wife of Leo the Great, made a request to Zeno concerning some matter, and he did not accept it,
she cast him down,
and set up her brother Basiliscus as king.
Now that Basiliscus, while residing in Heraclea, rebelled against Zeno,
and was proclaimed king,
and he made his son Marcus Caesar.
Then Zeno, fearing Verina lest she devise {OCR?} his murder,
fled to Isauria,
because he was from there.
And also his wife Argania,
that is, Ariadne,
fled to him secretly.
And Basiliscus and his son Marcus reigned two years,
and they behaved evilly.
For in the beginning he was devoted to the Orthodox faith,
and he restored the holy Timothy to Alexandria, and the bones of the ho[ly]
Dioscorus,
and he wrote an Encyclical and anathematized the Council of Chalcedon;
afterwards he changed his mind and proclaimed it [the Council].
And when the fickleness of his mind was revealed,
Zeno was emboldened,
and gathered an army and came against him.
Then he [Basiliscus] sent Harmatius the general to fight with him.
Zeno, however, sent secretly to Harmatius and swore to him
that he would make his son Caesar,
and him general [magister militum].
And so Harmatius betrayed his master,
and united with Zeno,
and they entered Constantinople.
Basiliscus, however, {corrupt OCR text referring to Eutyches and Dioscorus whose teaching...}.
